comment: Rows deliberately DELETED from the opportunities table by an operator. Deletion removes them from url_dedupe's pool, so the scraper would re-insert them on the next run that finds the same URL; this file puts them back into the dedupe pool as tombstones. Prefer the console's reject/duplicate actions over SQL DELETE — rejected rows keep blocking by themselves and never need an entry here. Matching is by normalized URL AND similar name, exactly like the live dedupe, so a program re-found at a NEW url is not blocked. NOTE: entries for the ec18420-ec18518 id range were recovered from the opportunities.json backup or from dup_candidates copies (the 08-20 snapshot's date-only filename was overwritten by a same-day run, so that file does not describe these DB ids); ids with no authoritative record were dropped rather than tombstoned blind.
